subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Unit 2 – Lesson 6: English in action (Borrowing things)
outcomes: I can borrow things politely in English.
I can blend words like chain, sport and broom.
I can use our, their, when and why.

tf.s: We say "These are my books" for many books.
tf.why: Use "These are" for more than one thing.
For many books we say "These are my books."

tf.s: "Can I borrow it, please?" is a polite question.
A good answer to "Can I borrow it, please?" is "Yes. Here you are."
tf.why: "Here you are" means you give the thing.

tf.s: ch + ai + n makes the word "chain".
br + oo + m makes the word "boom".
"Hook" has the same middle sound as "book".
tf.why: Hook and book both have the short oo sound.

tf.s: "Spoon" has the same middle sound as "book".
tf.why: Spoon sounds like moon, not book.
We use "Why" to ask the reason.

tf.s: We say "This is my ruler" for one ruler.

boxes.why: One ruler: This is my ruler.
Many crayons: These are my crayons.

boxes.q: Reply: Can I borrow it, please?
boxes.why: We give the thing and say "Here you are."

boxes.q: Which word has the oo of "moon"?
boxes.why: Boot has the long oo like moon.

boxes.q: Find the odd sound: spoon, boot, cook
boxes.why: Cook has the short oo like book.

mcq.q: Which question do we use to borrow something?
mcq.why: "Can I borrow it, please?" asks for a thing politely.

mcq.q: What do we say when we give something?
Which is a tricky word from this lesson?
mcq.why: Our, their, when and why are the tricky words.

mcq.q: Which word has the sounds ch-ai-n?
You have many books. What do you say?
Your friend asks: Is this your pen? It is your pen. You say:
mcq.why: Answer a yes question with "Yes, it is."

mcq.q: Complete: It is ___ book. (the book of you and me)
Which word does NOT have the same oo sound as the others?
mcq.why: Cook has the short oo; the others have the long oo.

mcq.q: Sara wants Ali's ruler. What is the most polite way to ask?
mcq.why: Polite words like "please" show good manners.

mcq.q: Why do we say "These are" and not "This is" for crayons?
mcq.why: "These are" is for more than one thing.
